originalFormat: Single-file .glb (obj2gltf-generated, Poly Pizza's standard conversion pipeline), downloaded as-is

validation.note: Single mesh, 5 flat-color materials (no baked textures), 2610 triangles per poly.pizza's listed Tris count. Bounding box is sane and near-origin (no corruption). Unit scale not independently confirmed against a real soroban (~30-45cm typical) -- if unit=meters this reads oversized (~65cm x 15cm x 80cm); re-check/rescale before placing in a scene.

reviewNote: Passed structural/header validation only (magic header, chunk parse, declared-length match, sane near-origin bounding box). Not yet opened in a 3D viewer or screenshotted. Do not treat as visually approved.
mappedComponent: math/number-and-arithmetic/abacus -- resolves the sourcing gap flagged in docs/assets/math.md wave 1 (5b). Wave 1 found a license-qualifying abacus on Sketchfab (pamruta, CC-BY) but could not download it because Sketchfab gates all downloads behind an OAuth account this environment does not have. This is a different, independently-found abacus on Poly Pizza, downloadable with no auth wall, so it was actually retrieved this wave.
notes: Real soroban abacus: wooden hinged case, visible bead rods. Single mesh / single node (case + frame + beads are not separated into individually addressable nodes), so per wave1's own assessment this is best used as a static reference/compare model (isolate + rotate) rather than a drag-interactive manipulative -- an interactive bead-slide abacus with named Rod_1..Rod_10 / Bead_* nodes would still need to be a procedural-script build to get the house hotspot/interaction contract, consistent with math.json's other 43 authored Math components.
